sanskrit: īśānaḥ prāṇadaḥ prāṇo jyeṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ hiraṇyagarbho bhūgarbho mādhavo madhusūdanaḥ
english: He is Īśāna, the supreme ruler; Prāṇada, giver of life; Prāṇa, the breath of life; Jyeṣṭha, the eldest; Śreṣṭha, the most excellent; Prajāpati, lord of creatures; Hiraṇyagarbha, the golden womb; Bhūgarbha, in whose womb the earth abides; Mādhava, lord of fortune; and Madhusūdana, slayer of Madhu.

sanskrit: īśvaro vikramī dhanvī medhāvī vikramaḥ kramaḥ anuttamo durādharṣaḥ kṛtajñaḥ kṛtir ātmavān
english: He is Īśvara, the lord; Vikramī, the valiant; Dhanvī, the bearer of the bow; Medhāvī, the wise; Vikrama, valor itself; Krama, the strider; Anuttama, than whom none is higher; Durādharṣa, unassailable; Kṛtajña, knower of all that is done; Kṛti, the doer of deeds; and Ātmavān, master of himself.

sanskrit: sureśaḥ śaraṇaṃ śarma viśvaretāḥ prajābhavaḥ ahaḥ saṃvatsaro vyālaḥ pratyayaḥ sarvadarśanaḥ
english: He is Sureśa, lord of the gods; Śaraṇa, the refuge; Śarma, supreme bliss; Viśvaretas, the seed of the universe; Prajābhava, the source of all beings; Aha, the day; Saṃvatsara, the year; Vyāla, the elusive serpent; Pratyaya, the ground of certainty; and Sarvadarśana, the all-seeing.

sanskrit: ajaḥ sarveśvaraḥ siddhaḥ siddhiḥ sarvādir acyutaḥ vṛṣākapir ameyātmā sarvayogaviniḥsṛtaḥ
english: He is Aja, the unborn; Sarveśvara, lord of all; Siddha, the perfected; Siddhi, attainment itself; Sarvādi, the beginning of all; Acyuta, the unfallen; Vṛṣākapi, the boar of righteousness; Ameyātmā, of immeasurable being; and Sarvayogaviniḥsṛta, who issues forth from all union.

sanskrit: vasur vasumanāḥ satyaḥ samātmā saṃmitaḥ samaḥ amoghaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣo vṛṣakarmā vṛṣākṛtiḥ
english: He is Vasu, the abode of all; Vasumanas, of generous mind; Satya, the truth; Samātmā, even-souled; Saṃmita, well-measured; Sama, the impartial; Amogha, whose deeds are never in vain; Puṇḍarīkākṣa, the lotus-eyed; Vṛṣakarmā, whose deeds are righteous; and Vṛṣākṛti, the very form of dharma.

sanskrit: rudro bahuśirā babhrur viśvayoniḥ śuciśravāḥ amṛtaḥ śāśvataḥ sthāṇur varāroho mahātapāḥ
english: He is Rudra, the terrible; Bahuśiras, the many-headed; Babhru, the upholder; Viśvayoni, the womb of the universe; Śuciśravas, of pure renown; Amṛta, the immortal; Śāśvata, the everlasting; Sthāṇu, the firm and unmoving; Varāroha, the supreme ascent; and Mahātapas, of mighty austerity.

sanskrit: sarvagaḥ sarvavid bhānur viṣvakseno janārdanaḥ vedo vedavid avyaṅgo vedāṅgo vedavit kaviḥ
english: He is Sarvaga, the all-pervading; Sarvavid, the all-knowing; Bhānu, the radiant; Viṣvaksena, before whose marshalled hosts the foe scatters; Janārdana, who afflicts the wicked; Veda, the sacred knowledge; Vedavid, the knower of the Vedas; Avyaṅga, the flawless; Vedāṅga, whose limbs are the Vedas; Vedavit, the knower of the Veda; and Kavi, the seer-poet.

sanskrit: lokādhyakṣaḥ surādhyakṣo dharmādhyakṣaḥ kṛtākṛtaḥ caturātmā caturvyūhaś caturdaṃṣṭraś caturbhujaḥ
english: He is Lokādhyakṣa, overseer of the worlds; Surādhyakṣa, overseer of the gods; Dharmādhyakṣa, overseer of dharma; Kṛtākṛta, both the effect and its cause; Caturātmā, of fourfold self; Caturvyūha, of fourfold manifestation; Caturdaṃṣṭra, the four-tusked; and Caturbhuja, the four-armed.

sanskrit: bhrājiṣṇur bhojanaṃ bhoktā sahiṣṇur jagadādijaḥ anagho vijayo jetā viśvayoniḥ punarvasuḥ
english: He is Bhrājiṣṇu, the ever-shining; Bhojana, the object of enjoyment; Bhoktā, the enjoyer; Sahiṣṇu, the all-enduring; Jagadādija, born at the beginning of the world; Anagha, the sinless; Vijaya, victory itself; Jetā, the conqueror; Viśvayoni, the womb of the universe; and Punarvasu, who dwells again and again within all.

sanskrit: upendro vāmanaḥ prāṃśur amoghaḥ śucir ūrjitaḥ atīndraḥ saṃgrahaḥ sargo dhṛtātmā niyamo yamaḥ
english: He is Upendra, the younger of Indra; Vāmana, the dwarf; Prāṃśu, the towering; Amogha, the unerring; Śuci, the pure; Ūrjita, of mighty strength; Atīndra, who surpasses Indra; Saṃgraha, the gatherer of all; Sarga, creation itself; Dhṛtātmā, the self-sustained; Niyama, the appointing power; and Yama, the restrainer.

sanskrit: vedyo vaidyaḥ sadāyogī vīrahā mādhavo madhuḥ atīndriyo mahāmāyo mahotsāho mahābalaḥ
english: He is Vedya, the one to be known; Vaidya, the wise physician; Sadāyogī, ever united in yoga; Vīrahā, slayer of mighty foes; Mādhava, lord of knowledge; Madhu, the sweetness of nectar; Atīndriya, beyond the senses; Mahāmāya, of great wondrous power; Mahotsāha, of mighty energy; and Mahābala, of great strength.

sanskrit: mahābuddhir mahāvīryo mahāśaktir mahādyutiḥ anirdeśyavapuḥ śrīmān ameyātmā mahādridhṛk
english: He is Mahābuddhi, of great intelligence; Mahāvīrya, of great virility; Mahāśakti, of great power; Mahādyuti, of great splendor; Anirdeśyavapus, whose form cannot be defined; Śrīmān, the glorious; Ameyātmā, of immeasurable being; and Mahādridhṛk, who upheld the great mountain.

sanskrit: maheṣvāso mahībhartā śrīnivāsaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ aniruddhaḥ surānando govindo govidāṃ patiḥ
english: He is Maheṣvāsa, the mighty archer; Mahībhartā, the upholder of the earth; Śrīnivāsa, the abode of Śrī; Satāṃ gati, the refuge of the good; Aniruddha, the unobstructed; Surānanda, the joy of the gods; Govinda, the keeper of cows and finder of the earth; and Govidāṃ pati, lord of those who know the words of wisdom.

sanskrit: marīcir damano haṃsaḥ suparṇo bhujagottamaḥ hiraṇyanābhaḥ sutapāḥ padmanābhaḥ prajāpatiḥ
english: He is Marīci, the ray of light; Damana, the subduer; Haṃsa, the swan of the soul; Suparṇa, the fair-winged; Bhujagottama, best of serpents; Hiraṇyanābha, the golden-naveled; Sutapas, of perfect austerity; Padmanābha, the lotus-naveled; and Prajāpati, lord of creatures.

sanskrit: amṛtyuḥ sarvadṛk siṃhaḥ saṃdhātā saṃdhimān sthiraḥ ajo durmarṣaṇaḥ śāstā viśrutātmā surārihā
english: He is Amṛtyu, the deathless; Sarvadṛk, the all-seeing; Siṃha, the lion; Saṃdhātā, who joins and ordains; Saṃdhimān, who abides by his bonds; Sthira, the steadfast; Aja, the unborn; Durmarṣaṇa, who cannot be borne by foes; Śāstā, the chastiser and teacher; Viśrutātmā, of famed renown; and Surārihā, slayer of the enemies of the gods.

sanskrit: gurur gurutamo dhāma satyaḥ satyaparākramaḥ nimiṣo 'nimiṣaḥ sragvī vācaspatir udāradhīḥ
english: He is Guru, the teacher; Gurutama, the highest of teachers; Dhāma, the supreme abode; Satya, the true; Satyaparākrama, of true and tireless valor; Nimiṣa, who closes his eyes in cosmic sleep; Animiṣa, the ever-wakeful; Sragvī, garlanded; Vācaspati, lord of speech; and Udāradhī, of noble intellect.

sanskrit: agraṇīr grāmaṇīḥ śrīmān nyāyo netā samīraṇaḥ sahasramūrdhā viśvātmā sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt
english: He is Agraṇī, the foremost leader; Grāmaṇī, the guide of the multitude; Śrīmān, the glorious; Nyāya, justice itself; Netā, the leader; Samīraṇa, the moving wind; Sahasramūrdhā, the thousand-headed; Viśvātmā, the soul of the universe; Sahasrākṣa, the thousand-eyed; and Sahasrapāt, the thousand-footed.

sanskrit: āvartano nivṛttātmā saṃvṛtaḥ saṃpramardanaḥ ahaḥ saṃvartako vahnir anilo dharaṇīdharaḥ
english: He is Āvartana, who turns the wheel of being; Nivṛttātmā, the soul turned away from the world; Saṃvṛta, the enveloped and hidden; Saṃpramardana, the great crusher of foes; Ahassaṃvartaka, who sets the days revolving; Vahni, the bearer of oblations as fire; Anila, the wind; and Dharaṇīdhara, the upholder of the earth.

sanskrit: suprasādaḥ prasannātmā viśvadhṛg viśvabhug vibhuḥ satkartā satkṛtaḥ sādhur jahnur nārāyaṇo naraḥ
english: He is Suprasāda, the gracious; Prasannātmā, of serene soul; Viśvadhṛk, who upholds the universe; Viśvabhuk, who enjoys all worlds; Vibhu, the omnipresent; Satkartā, the honorer of the good; Satkṛta, who is honored; Sādhu, the righteous; Jahnu, who withdraws all beings; Nārāyaṇa, who dwells upon the waters; and Nara, the eternal Man.

sanskrit: asaṃkhyeyo 'prameyātmā viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭakṛc chuciḥ siddhārthaḥ siddhasaṃkalpaḥ siddhidaḥ siddhisādhanaḥ
english: He is Asaṃkhyeya, the innumerable; Aprameyātmā, of immeasurable being; Viśiṣṭa, the most excellent; Śiṣṭakṛt, who lays down the law for the righteous; Śuci, the pure; Siddhārtha, whose every purpose is fulfilled; Siddhasaṃkalpa, whose resolves come to pass; Siddhida, the giver of perfection; and Siddhisādhana, the means to all attainment.

sanskrit: vṛṣāhī vṛṣabho viṣṇur vṛṣaparvā vṛṣodaraḥ vardhano vardhamānaś ca viviktaḥ śrutisāgaraḥ
english: He is Vṛṣāhī, whose days are righteousness; Vṛṣabha, the bull of dharma; Viṣṇu, the all-pervading; Vṛṣaparvā, the ladder of righteousness; Vṛṣodara, from whose belly all beings spring; Vardhana, who makes all flourish; Vardhamāna, the ever-increasing; Vivikta, the unmingled and aloof; and Śrutisāgara, the ocean of sacred scripture.

sanskrit: subhujo durdharo vāgmī mahendro vasudo vasuḥ naikarūpo bṛhadrūpaḥ śipiviṣṭaḥ prakāśanaḥ
english: He is Subhuja, the fair-armed; Durdhara, hard to hold or bear; Vāgmī, the eloquent; Mahendra, the great lord; Vasuda, the giver of wealth; Vasu, wealth itself; Naikarūpa, of manifold forms; Bṛhadrūpa, of vast form; Śipiviṣṭa, who dwells within the rays; and Prakāśana, the illuminator.

sanskrit: ojas tejo dyutidharaḥ prakāśātmā pratāpanaḥ ṛddhaḥ spaṣṭākṣaro mantraś candrāṃśur bhāskaradyutiḥ
english: He is Ojastejodyutidhara, who holds vital force, splendor, and brilliance; Prakāśātmā, of luminous self; Pratāpana, who blazes forth heat; Ṛddha, the abounding; Spaṣṭākṣara, made manifest in the syllable Oṃ; Mantra, the sacred utterance; Candrāṃśu, ray of the moon; and Bhāskaradyuti, with the radiance of the sun.

sanskrit: amṛtāṃśūdbhavo bhānuḥ śaśabinduḥ sureśvaraḥ auṣadhaṃ jagataḥ setuḥ satyadharmaparākramaḥ
english: He is Amṛtāṃśūdbhava, from whom the nectar-rayed moon arose; Bhānu, the shining; Śaśabindu, the hare-marked moon; Sureśvara, lord of the gods; Auṣadha, the healing herb; Jagataḥsetu, the bridge across the world; and Satyadharmaparākrama, whose valor is truth and righteousness.

sanskrit: bhūtabhavyabhavannāthaḥ pavanaḥ pāvano 'nilaḥ kāmahā kāmakṛt kāntaḥ kāmaḥ kāmapradaḥ prabhuḥ
english: He is Bhūtabhavyabhavannātha, lord of past, future, and present; Pavana, the wind; Pāvana, the purifier; Anila, the breath that needs no support; Kāmahā, destroyer of desire; Kāmakṛt, fulfiller of desire; Kānta, the beautiful and beloved; Kāma, desire itself; Kāmaprada, the granter of wishes; and Prabhu, the lord.

sanskrit: yugādikṛd yugāvarto naikamāyo mahāśanaḥ adṛśyo vyaktarūpaś ca sahasrajid anantajit
english: He is Yugādikṛt, the maker of the ages' beginning; Yugāvarta, who turns the cycle of yugas; Naikamāya, of manifold illusion; Mahāśana, the great devourer; Adṛśya, the invisible; Vyaktarūpa, of manifest form; Sahasrajit, conqueror of thousands; and Anantajit, the ever-victorious.

sanskrit: iṣṭo viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ śikhaṇḍī nahuṣo vṛṣaḥ krodhahā krodhakṛt kartā viśvabāhur mahīdharaḥ
english: He is Iṣṭa, the beloved; Viśiṣṭa, the most excellent; Śiṣṭeṣṭa, dear to the righteous; Śikhaṇḍī, the crested one; Nahuṣa, who binds all beings; Vṛṣa, the embodiment of dharma; Krodhahā, slayer of wrath; Krodhakṛt, who rouses wrath against the wicked; Kartā, the doer; Viśvabāhu, of universal arms; and Mahīdhara, the upholder of the earth.

sanskrit: acyutaḥ prathitaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇado vāsavānujaḥ apāṃ nidhir adhiṣṭhānam apramattaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: He is Acyuta, the unfallen; Prathita, the renowned; Prāṇa, the breath of life; Prāṇada, giver of life; Vāsavānuja, the younger brother of Indra; Apāṃ nidhi, the treasure-house of the waters; Adhiṣṭhāna, the foundation of all; Apramatta, the ever-vigilant; and Pratiṣṭhita, the self-established.

sanskrit: skandaḥ skandadharo dhuryo varado vāyuvāhanaḥ vāsudevo bṛhadbhānur ādidevaḥ puraṃdaraḥ
english: He is Skanda, who flows forth as nectar; Skandadhara, upholder of the path of dharma; Dhurya, who bears the yoke of creation; Varada, the granter of boons; Vāyuvāhana, who drives the winds; Vāsudeva, the indwelling and all-pervading; Bṛhadbhānu, of vast radiance; Ādideva, the primeval god; and Puraṃdara, the breaker of strongholds.

sanskrit: aśokas tāraṇas tāraḥ śūraḥ śaurir janeśvaraḥ anukūlaḥ śatāvartaḥ padmī padmanibhekṣaṇaḥ
english: He is Aśoka, the sorrowless; Tāraṇa, who ferries beings across; Tāra, the deliverer; Śūra, the hero; Śauri, born in the line of Śūra; Janeśvara, lord of men; Anukūla, the ever-favorable; Śatāvarta, of a hundred manifestations; Padmī, the lotus-holder; and Padmanibhekṣaṇa, whose eyes resemble lotuses.

sanskrit: padmanābho 'ravindākṣaḥ padmagarbhaḥ śarīrabhṛt maharddhir ṛddho vṛddhātmā mahākṣo garuḍadhvajaḥ
english: He is Padmanābha, the lotus-naveled; Aravindākṣa, the lotus-eyed; Padmagarbha, who is contemplated in the lotus of the heart; Śarīrabhṛt, the sustainer of bodies; Maharddhi, of great prosperity; Ṛddha, the abounding; Vṛddhātmā, the ancient soul; Mahākṣa, the great-eyed; and Garuḍadhvaja, who bears Garuḍa on his banner.

sanskrit: atulaḥ śarabho bhīmaḥ samayajño havir hariḥ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇyo lakṣmīvān samitiṃjayaḥ
english: He is Atula, the incomparable; Śarabha, who dwells within the body; Bhīma, the terrible; Samayajña, knower of the proper occasions; Havis, the oblation; Hari, the tawny and the remover of sin; Sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇya, known by every auspicious mark; Lakṣmīvān, the consort of Lakṣmī; and Samitiṃjaya, the victor in battle.

sanskrit: vikṣaro rohito mārgo hetur dāmodaraḥ sahaḥ mahīdharo mahābhāgo vegavān amitāśanaḥ
english: He is Vikṣara, the imperishable; Rohita, the assumer of forms like the fish; Mārga, the path; Hetu, the cause; Dāmodara, bound at the waist with a cord; Saha, the all-enduring; Mahīdhara, upholder of the earth; Mahābhāga, of great fortune; Vegavān, the swift; and Amitāśana, of boundless appetite.

sanskrit: udbhavaḥ kṣobhaṇo devaḥ śrīgarbhaḥ parameśvaraḥ karaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ kartā vikartā gahano guhaḥ
english: He is Udbhava, the source of all; Kṣobhaṇa, who stirred creation into being; Deva, the resplendent; Śrīgarbha, in whose womb all glory abides; Parameśvara, the supreme lord; Karaṇa, the instrument; Kāraṇa, the cause; Kartā, the doer; Vikartā, the maker of manifold worlds; Gahana, the unfathomable; and Guha, the hidden one.

sanskrit: vyavasāyo vyavasthānaḥ saṃsthānaḥ sthānado dhruvaḥ pararddhiḥ paramaḥ spaṣṭas tuṣṭaḥ puṣṭaḥ śubhekṣaṇaḥ
english: He is Vyavasāya, resolute knowledge; Vyavasthāna, the ordainer of order; Saṃsthāna, the final dissolution; Sthānada, the giver of abodes; Dhruva, the immovable; Pararddhi, of supreme prosperity; Parama, the highest; Spaṣṭa, the manifest; Tuṣṭa, the contented; Puṣṭa, the full; and Śubhekṣaṇa, of auspicious gaze.

sanskrit: rāmo virāmo virato mārgo neyo nayo 'nayaḥ vīraḥ śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭho dharmo dharmavid uttamaḥ
english: He is Rāma, the delightful; Virāma, the end and cessation; Virāṭa, the desireless; Mārga, the path; Neya, who is to be guided to by wisdom; Naya, the guide; Anaya, who needs no guide; Vīra, the hero; Śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭha, foremost of the powerful; Dharma, righteousness; Dharmavid uttama, the highest knower of dharma.

sanskrit: vaikuṇṭhaḥ puruṣaḥ prāṇaḥ prāṇadaḥ praṇavaḥ pṛthuḥ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ śatrughno vyāpto vāyur adhokṣajaḥ
english: He is Vaikuṇṭha, who unites the scattered worlds; Puruṣa, the cosmic Person; Prāṇa, the breath of life; Prāṇada, the giver of life; Praṇava, the sacred Oṃ; Pṛthu, the vast and expanded; Hiraṇyagarbha, the golden womb; Śatrughna, slayer of foes; Vyāpta, the all-pervading; Vāyu, the wind; and Adhokṣaja, who never declines from his own nature.

sanskrit: ṛtuḥ sudarśanaḥ kālaḥ parameṣṭhī parigrahaḥ ugraḥ saṃvatsaro dakṣo viśrāmo viśvadakṣiṇaḥ
english: He is Ṛtu, the season; Sudarśana, of fair vision; Kāla, time itself; Parameṣṭhī, established on high; Parigraha, the receiver and embracer of all; Ugra, the formidable; Saṃvatsara, the year; Dakṣa, the able and swift; Viśrāma, the place of rest; and Viśvadakṣiṇa, skillful in all things and most liberal.

sanskrit: vistāraḥ sthāvaraḥ sthāṇuḥ pramāṇaṃ bījam avyayam artho 'nartho mahākośo mahābhogo mahādhanaḥ
english: He is Vistāra, the expanse in which all worlds abide; Sthāvarasthāṇu, the firm and unmoving ground; Pramāṇa, the measure and proof of all; Bīja avyaya, the imperishable seed; Artha, the goal of all desire; Anartha, who has no want of his own; Mahākośa, the great treasury; Mahābhoga, of great enjoyment; and Mahādhana, of great wealth.

sanskrit: anirviṇṇaḥ sthaviṣṭho bhūr dharmayūpo mahāmakhaḥ nakṣatranemir nakṣatrī kṣamaḥ kṣāmaḥ samīhanaḥ
english: He is Anirviṇṇa, the never-despondent; Sthaviṣṭha, the most massive; Bhū, the abode of being; Dharmayūpa, the sacrificial post of righteousness; Mahāmakha, the great sacrifice; Nakṣatranemi, the hub of the stars; Nakṣatrī, the lord of constellations; Kṣama, the all-capable; Kṣāma, who abides when all is dissolved; and Samīhana, who wills the good of all.

sanskrit: yajña ijyo mahejyaś ca kratuḥ satraṃ satāṃ gatiḥ sarvadarśī vimuktātmā sarvajño jñānam uttamam
english: He is Yajña, the sacrifice; Ijya, the one to be worshipped; Mahejya, supremely worshipped; Kratu, the rite; Satra, the prolonged offering; Satāṃ gati, the refuge of the good; Sarvadarśī, the all-seeing; Vimuktātmā, the ever-liberated soul; Sarvajña, the omniscient; and Jñānam uttamam, the highest knowledge.

sanskrit: suvrataḥ sumukhaḥ sūkṣmaḥ sughoṣaḥ sukhadaḥ suhṛt manoharo jitakrodho vīrabāhur vidāraṇaḥ
english: He is Suvrata, of holy vows; Sumukha, of fair countenance; Sūkṣma, the subtle; Sughoṣa, of auspicious sound; Sukhada, the giver of joy; Suhṛt, the true friend; Manohara, the captivator of the mind; Jitakrodha, conqueror of wrath; Vīrabāhu, of heroic arms; and Vidāraṇa, the render of the wicked.

sanskrit: svāpanaḥ svavaśo vyāpī naikātmā naikakarmakṛt vatsaro vatsalo vatsī ratnagarbho dhaneśvaraḥ
english: He is Svāpana, who casts beings into the sleep of ignorance; Svavaśa, subject to none but himself; Vyāpī, the all-pervading; Naikātmā, of manifold selves; Naikakarmakṛt, the doer of countless deeds; Vatsara, the abode of all; Vatsala, the affectionate; Vatsī, the loving father; Ratnagarbha, in whose womb lie all jewels; and Dhaneśvara, lord of wealth.

sanskrit: dharmagub dharmakṛd dharmī sad asat kṣaram akṣaram avijñātā sahasrāṃśur vidhātā kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ
english: He is Dharmagub, the protector of dharma; Dharmakṛt, the doer of righteousness; Dharmī, the upholder of dharma; Sat, the existent; Asat, the non-existent; Kṣara, the perishable; Akṣara, the imperishable; Avijñātā, who is beyond all knowing; Sahasrāṃśu, the thousand-rayed; Vidhātā, the ordainer; and Kṛtalakṣaṇa, who has fixed the marks of all.

sanskrit: gabhastinemiḥ sattvasthaḥ siṃho bhūtamaheśvaraḥ ādidevo mahādevo deveśo devabhṛd guruḥ
english: He is Gabhastinemi, the hub at the center of the rays; Sattvastha, abiding in the heart of all beings; Siṃha, the lion; Bhūtamaheśvara, the great lord of beings; Ādideva, the primeval god; Mahādeva, the great god; Deveśa, lord of the gods; Devabhṛt, the upholder of the gods; and Guru, the teacher.

sanskrit: uttaro gopatir goptā jñānagamyaḥ purātanaḥ śarīrabhūtabhṛd bhoktā kapīndro bhūridakṣiṇaḥ
english: He is Uttara, who lifts beings out of the ocean of being; Gopati, lord of the earth and of cows; Goptā, the protector; Jñānagamya, to be reached by wisdom; Purātana, the ancient; Śarīrabhūtabhṛt, who upholds the elements of the body; Bhoktā, the enjoyer; Kapīndra, lord of monkeys as Rāma; and Bhūridakṣiṇa, of abundant sacrificial gifts.

sanskrit: somapo 'mṛtapaḥ somaḥ purujit purusattamaḥ vinayo jayaḥ satyasaṃdho dāśārhaḥ sātvatāṃ patiḥ
english: He is Somapa, the drinker of soma; Amṛtapa, the drinker of nectar; Soma, the moon that nourishes the herbs; Purujit, conqueror of many; Purusattama, supreme among beings; Vinaya, who humbles the proud; Jaya, victory; Satyasaṃdha, true to his word; Dāśārha, worthy of all offerings; and Sātvatāṃ pati, lord of the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: jīvo vinayitā sākṣī mukundo 'mitavikramaḥ ambhonidhir anantātmā mahodadhiśayo 'ntakaḥ
english: He is Jīva, the living soul; Vinayitā, the bestower of discipline; Sākṣī, the witness; Mukunda, the giver of liberation; Amitavikrama, of measureless valor; Ambhonidhi, the treasure-house of waters; Anantātmā, of infinite being; Mahodadhiśaya, who reposes upon the great ocean; and Antaka, the maker of the end.

sanskrit: ajo mahārhaḥ svābhāvyo jitāmitraḥ pramodanaḥ ānando nandano nandaḥ satyadharmā trivikramaḥ
english: He is Aja, the unborn; Mahārha, supremely worthy of worship; Svābhāvya, established in his own nature; Jitāmitra, conqueror of foes; Pramodana, the giver of joy; Ānanda, bliss itself; Nandana, the delighter; Nanda, the abounding in joy; Satyadharmā, whose dharma is truth; and Trivikrama, who strode across the three worlds.

sanskrit: maharṣiḥ kapilācāryaḥ kṛtajño medinīpatiḥ tripadas tridaśādhyakṣo mahāśṛṅgaḥ kṛtāntakṛt
english: He is Maharṣi Kapilācārya, the great seer who taught as Kapila; Kṛtajña, knower of all that is wrought; Medinīpati, lord of the earth; Tripada, the three-stepped; Tridaśādhyakṣa, overseer of the thirty gods; Mahāśṛṅga, the great-horned who saved the Vedas; and Kṛtāntakṛt, the maker of all ends.

sanskrit: mahāvarāho govindaḥ suṣeṇaḥ kanakāṅgadī guhyo gabhīro gahano guptaś cakragadādharaḥ
english: He is Mahāvarāha, the great boar; Govinda, the finder of the earth; Suṣeṇa, of goodly hosts; Kanakāṅgadī, adorned with golden armlets; Guhya, the secret one; Gabhīra, the profound; Gahana, the unfathomable; Gupta, the hidden; and Cakragadādhara, the bearer of discus and mace.

sanskrit: vedhāḥ svāṅgo 'jitaḥ kṛṣṇo dṛḍhaḥ saṃkarṣaṇo 'cyutaḥ varuṇo vāruṇo vṛkṣaḥ puṣkarākṣo mahāmanāḥ
english: He is Vedhā, the creator; Svāṅga, who is his own instrument; Ajita, the unconquered; Kṛṣṇa, the dark and all-attracting; Dṛḍha, the firm; Saṃkarṣaṇa, who draws all beings into himself; Acyuta, the unfallen; Varuṇa, who gathers his rays at evening; Vāruṇa, son of Varuṇa as Vasiṣṭha; Vṛkṣa, the tree that stands unshaken; Puṣkarākṣa, the lotus-eyed; and Mahāmanas, of vast mind.

sanskrit: bhagavān bhagahā nandī vanamālī halāyudhaḥ ādityo jyotir ādityaḥ sahiṣṇur gatisattamaḥ
english: He is Bhagavān, the blessed lord of the six excellences; Bhagahā, who withdraws those powers at dissolution; Nandī, ever joyful; Vanamālī, wearer of the forest garland; Halāyudha, who wields the plow as Balarāma; Āditya, the son of Aditi; Jyotirāditya, the radiance within the orb of the sun; Sahiṣṇu, the all-enduring; and Gatisattama, the supreme refuge.

sanskrit: sudhanvā khaṇḍaparaśur dāruṇo draviṇapradaḥ divaḥspṛk sarvadṛg vyāso vācaspatir ayonijaḥ
english: He is Sudhanvā, of the goodly bow; Khaṇḍaparaśu, who bore the battle-axe as Rāma Jāmadagnya; Dāruṇa, the merciless to the wicked; Draviṇaprada, the giver of riches; Divaḥspṛk, who touches the heavens; Sarvadṛk, the all-seeing; Vyāsa, the arranger of the Vedas; Vācaspati, lord of speech; and Ayonija, who is born of no womb.

sanskrit: trisāmā sāmagaḥ sāma nirvāṇaṃ bheṣajaṃ bhiṣak saṃnyāsakṛc chamaḥ śānto niṣṭhā śāntiḥ parāyaṇam
english: He is Trisāmā, hymned by the three Sāmans; Sāmaga, the singer of the Sāman; Sāma, the chant itself; Nirvāṇa, supreme extinction in bliss; Bheṣaja, the medicine; Bhiṣak, the physician; Saṃnyāsakṛt, who ordained renunciation; Śama, tranquility; Śānta, the peaceful; Niṣṭhā, the final ground; Śānti, peace itself; and Parāyaṇa, the supreme goal.

sanskrit: śubhāṅgaḥ śāntidaḥ sraṣṭā kumudaḥ kuvaleśayaḥ gohito gopatir goptā vṛṣabhākṣo vṛṣapriyaḥ
english: He is Śubhāṅga, of beautiful form; Śāntida, the giver of peace; Sraṣṭā, the creator; Kumuda, who delights in the earth; Kuvaleśaya, who reposes upon the waters; Gohita, the well-doer of the earth and cattle; Gopati, lord of the earth; Goptā, the protector; Vṛṣabhākṣa, whose eyes rain down all desires; and Vṛṣapriya, the lover of righteousness.

sanskrit: anivartī nivṛttātmā saṃkṣeptā kṣemakṛc chivaḥ śrīvatsavakṣāḥ śrīvāsaḥ śrīpatiḥ śrīmatāṃ varaḥ
english: He is Anivartī, who never turns back from righteousness; Nivṛttātmā, the soul withdrawn from the world; Saṃkṣeptā, who draws the vast worlds together; Kṣemakṛt, the bestower of welfare; Śiva, the auspicious; Śrīvatsavakṣas, who bears the Śrīvatsa mark upon his breast; Śrīvāsa, the dwelling-place of Śrī; Śrīpati, lord of Śrī; and Śrīmatāṃ vara, foremost of the glorious.

sanskrit: śrīdaḥ śrīśaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīnidhiḥ śrīvibhāvanaḥ śrīdharaḥ śrīkaraḥ śreyaḥ śrīmāṃl lokatrayāśrayaḥ
english: He is Śrīda, the giver of fortune; Śrīśa, lord of Śrī; Śrīnivāsa, the abode of Śrī; Śrīnidhi, the treasury of glory; Śrīvibhāvana, the dispenser of fortune to all; Śrīdhara, who bears Śrī upon his breast; Śrīkara, the maker of prosperity; Śreyas, the highest good; Śrīmān, the glorious; and Lokatrayāśraya, the refuge of the three worlds.

sanskrit: svakṣaḥ svaṅgaḥ śatānando nandir jyotir gaṇeśvaraḥ vijitātmā vidheyātmā satkīrtiś chinnasaṃśayaḥ
english: He is Svakṣa, of beautiful eyes; Svaṅga, of fair limbs; Śatānanda, of a hundred joys; Nandi, supreme bliss; Jyotirgaṇeśvara, lord of the host of luminaries; Vijitātmā, who has conquered the self; Vidheyātmā, ever at his own command; Satkīrti, of true renown; and Chinnasaṃśaya, in whom all doubt is severed.

sanskrit: udīrṇaḥ sarvataścakṣur anīśaḥ śāśvataḥ sthiraḥ bhūśayo bhūṣaṇo bhūtir viśokaḥ śokanāśanaḥ
english: He is Udīrṇa, who transcends all beings; Sarvataścakṣus, whose eyes are turned in every direction; Anīśa, over whom there is no lord; Śāśvata, the everlasting; Sthira, the steadfast; Bhūśaya, who reposes upon the earth and the waters; Bhūṣaṇa, the ornament of the worlds; Bhūti, pure existence and prosperity; Viśoka, the sorrowless; and Śokanāśana, the destroyer of grief.

sanskrit: arciṣmān arcitaḥ kumbho viśuddhātmā viśodhanaḥ aniruddho 'pratirathaḥ pradyumno 'mitavikramaḥ
english: He is Arciṣmān, the effulgent; Arcita, the worshipped; Kumbha, the vessel in which all abides; Viśuddhātmā, of utterly pure self; Viśodhana, the purifier; Aniruddha, the unobstructed; Apratiratha, who has no equal foe; Pradyumna, of surpassing wealth; and Amitavikrama, of measureless valor.

sanskrit: kālaneminihā vīraḥ śūraḥ śaurir janeśvaraḥ trilokātmā trilokeśaḥ keśavaḥ keśihā hariḥ
english: He is Kālaneminihā, slayer of the demon Kālanemi; Vīra, the hero; Śūra, the valiant; Śauri, born in the line of Śūra; Janeśvara, lord of men; Trilokātmā, the soul of the three worlds; Trilokeśa, lord of the three worlds; Keśava, of beautiful locks and lord of Brahmā and Śiva; Keśihā, slayer of the demon Keśin; and Hari, the remover of sin.

sanskrit: kāmadevaḥ kāmapālaḥ kāmī kāntaḥ kṛtāgamaḥ anirdeśyavapur viṣṇur vīro 'nanto dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: He is Kāmadeva, the god of love and the object of all desire; Kāmapāla, the guardian of desires fulfilled; Kāmī, in whom all wishes are complete; Kānta, the beautiful; Kṛtāgama, the author of the sacred scriptures; Anirdeśyavapus, of indefinable form; Viṣṇu, the all-pervading; Vīra, the hero; Ananta, the infinite; and Dhanaṃjaya, the winner of wealth.

sanskrit: brahmaṇyo brahmakṛd brahmā brahma brahmavivardhanaḥ brahmavid brāhmaṇo brahmī brahmajño brāhmaṇapriyaḥ
english: He is Brahmaṇya, the well-wisher of Brahman and the brāhmaṇas; Brahmakṛt, the maker of sacred austerity; Brahmā, the creator; Brahmā, the absolute itself; Brahmavivardhana, who increases all that is holy; Brahmavid, the knower of Brahman; Brāhmaṇa, the proclaimer of the Veda; Brahmī, who possesses all sacred power; Brahmajña, the knower of Brahman; and Brāhmaṇapriya, dear to the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: mahākramo mahākarmā mahātejā mahoragaḥ mahākratur mahāyajvā mahāyajño mahāhaviḥ
english: He is Mahākrama, of mighty stride; Mahākarmā, of great deeds; Mahātejas, of great splendor; Mahoraga, the great serpent; Mahākratu, the great sacrifice; Mahāyajvā, the great performer of rites; Mahāyajña, the great offering; and Mahāhavis, the great oblation.

sanskrit: stavyaḥ stavapriyaḥ stotraṃ stutiḥ stotā raṇapriyaḥ pūrṇaḥ pūrayitā puṇyaḥ puṇyakīrtir anāmayaḥ
english: He is Stavya, the one to be praised; Stavapriya, who loves the hymns of praise; Stotra, the hymn itself; Stuti, the praise; Stotā, the praiser; Raṇapriya, who delights in battle; Pūrṇa, the all-complete; Pūrayitā, the fulfiller; Puṇya, the holy; Puṇyakīrti, of sacred renown; and Anāmaya, free from all affliction.

sanskrit: manojavas tīrthakaro vasuretā vasupradaḥ vasuprado vāsudevo vasur vasumanā haviḥ
english: He is Manojava, swift as thought; Tīrthakara, the maker of sacred fords of knowledge; Vasuretas, whose essence is golden; Vasuprada, the giver of wealth; again Vasuprada, the bestower of riches; Vāsudeva, the indwelling and all-pervading; Vasu, the abode of all; Vasumanas, of generous mind; and Havis, the oblation.

sanskrit: sadgatiḥ satkṛtiḥ sattā sadbhūtiḥ satparāyaṇaḥ śūraseno yaduśreṣṭhaḥ sannivāsaḥ suyāmunaḥ
english: He is Sadgati, the refuge of the good; Satkṛti, of righteous deeds; Sattā, pure existence; Sadbhūti, the abundance of being; Satparāyaṇa, the supreme goal of the virtuous; Śūrasena, of valiant armies; Yaduśreṣṭha, foremost of the Yadus; Sannivāsa, the abode of the good; and Suyāmuna, attended by the dwellers along the Yamunā.

sanskrit: bhūtāvāso vāsudevo sarvāsunilayo 'nalaḥ darpahā darpado dṛpto durdharo 'thāparājitaḥ
english: He is Bhūtāvāsa, the dwelling-place of all beings; Vāsudeva, who veils the worlds with his māyā; Sarvāsunilaya, the resting-place of all life-breaths; Anala, the fire and the never-sufficient; Darpahā, destroyer of the pride of the wicked; Darpada, who grants just pride to the righteous; Dṛpta, the ever-content; Durdhara, the hard to hold; and Aparājita, the unvanquished.

sanskrit: viśvamūrtir mahāmūrtir dīptamūrtir amūrtimān anekamūrtir avyaktaḥ śatamūrtiḥ śatānanaḥ
english: He is Viśvamūrti, whose form is the universe; Mahāmūrti, of vast form; Dīptamūrti, of blazing form; Amūrtimān, the formless; Anekamūrti, of countless forms; Avyakta, the unmanifest; Śatamūrti, of a hundred forms; and Śatānana, the hundred-faced.

sanskrit: eko naikaḥ savaḥ kaḥ kiṃ yat tat padam anuttamam lokabandhur lokanātho mādhavo bhaktavatsalaḥ
english: He is Eka, the one; Naika, the manifold; Sava, the sacrifice of soma; Ka, who is bliss; Kim, the one worthy to be inquired after; Yat, the self-existent; Tat, the That of which all is; Padam anuttamam, the supreme abode beyond which there is none; Lokabandhu, the kinsman of all the worlds; Lokanātha, lord of the worlds; Mādhava, lord of fortune; and Bhaktavatsala, tender toward his devotees.

sanskrit: suvarṇavarṇo hemāṅgo varāṅgaś candanāṅgadī vīrahā viṣamaḥ śūnyo ghṛtāśīr acalaś calaḥ
english: He is Suvarṇavarṇa, of golden hue; Hemāṅga, of golden body; Varāṅga, of beautiful limbs; Candanāṅgadī, adorned with sandal-scented armlets; Vīrahā, slayer of heroes among the foe; Viṣama, who has no equal; Śūnya, the void devoid of all attributes; Ghṛtāśīs, whose blessings never fail; Acala, the immovable; and Cala, the ever-moving.

sanskrit: amānī mānado mānyo lokasvāmī trilokadhṛk sumedhā medhajo dhanyaḥ satyamedhā dharādharaḥ
english: He is Amānī, free from all conceit; Mānada, who bestows honor and humbles the proud; Mānya, the venerable; Lokasvāmī, lord of the worlds; Trilokadhṛk, upholder of the three worlds; Sumedhā, of fine intelligence; Medhaja, born of sacrifice; Dhanya, the blessed; Satyamedhā, of unfailing wisdom; and Dharādhara, the bearer of the earth.

sanskrit: tejo vṛṣo dyutidharaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ pragraho nigraho 'vyagro naikaśṛṅgo gadāgrajaḥ
english: He is Tejovṛṣa, who showers down splendor; Dyutidhara, the bearer of brilliance; Sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ vara, foremost of all who bear arms; Pragraha, the receiver of his devotees' offerings; Nigraha, who holds all in his grasp; Avyagra, the undistracted; Naikaśṛṅga, of manifold horns; and Gadāgraja, the elder brother of Gada, made manifest by the sacred syllable.

sanskrit: caturmūrtiś caturbāhuś caturvyūhaś caturgatiḥ caturātmā caturbhāvaś caturvedavid ekapāt
english: He is Caturmūrti, of fourfold form; Caturbāhu, the four-armed; Caturvyūha, of fourfold manifestation; Caturgati, the fourfold goal of beings; Caturātmā, of fourfold self; Caturbhāva, the source of the four orders of life; Caturvedavid, knower of the four Vedas; and Ekapāt, the single-footed who stands above all with the rest of his being.

sanskrit: samāvarto nivṛttātmā durjayo duratikramaḥ durlabho durgamo durgo durāvāso durārihā
english: He is Samāvarta, the skilled turner of the wheel of being; Nivṛttātmā, the soul withdrawn from the world; Durjaya, hard to conquer; Duratikrama, hard to transgress; Durlabha, hard to attain; Durgama, hard to approach; Durgā, the impassable; Durāvāsa, hard for the yogins to enshrine within; and Durārihā, slayer of dangerous foes.

sanskrit: śubhāṅgo lokasāraṅgaḥ sutantus tantuvardhanaḥ indrakarmā mahākarmā kṛtakarmā kṛtāgamaḥ
english: He is Śubhāṅga, of auspicious form; Lokasāraṅga, who draws forth the essence of the worlds; Sutantu, of beautiful weave who spread out the universe; Tantuvardhana, who extends or withdraws that weave; Indrakarmā, whose deeds are like Indra's; Mahākarmā, of mighty deeds; Kṛtakarmā, whose work is accomplished; and Kṛtāgama, the author of the sacred lore.

sanskrit: udbhavaḥ sundaraḥ sundo ratnanābhaḥ sulocanaḥ arko vājasanaḥ śṛṅgī jayantaḥ sarvavij jayī
english: He is Udbhava, the supreme source; Sundara, the beautiful; Sunda, of tender compassion; Ratnanābha, of jewel-like navel; Sulocana, of lovely eyes; Arka, the worshipful sun; Vājasana, the giver of food and sustenance; Śṛṅgī, the horned one who became the fish; Jayanta, the all-victorious; Sarvavid, the all-knowing; and Jayī, the ever-conquering.

sanskrit: suvarṇabindur akṣobhyaḥ sarvavāg īśvareśvaraḥ mahāhrado mahāgarto mahābhūto mahānidhiḥ
english: He is Suvarṇabindu, of golden-hued limbs; Akṣobhya, the unshakable; Sarvavāgīśvareśvara, lord of all lords of speech; Mahāhrada, the great deep wherein the yogins find delight; Mahāgarta, the great chasm and ground of all; Mahābhūta, the great being beyond all elements; and Mahānidhi, the great treasure in which the worlds repose.

sanskrit: kumudaḥ kuṃdaraḥ kundaḥ parjanyaḥ pavano 'nilaḥ amṛtāṃśo 'mṛtavapuḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ
english: He is Kumuda, who gladdens the earth; Kuṃdara, who cleaves the earth as the boar; Kunda, fair as the jasmine; Parjanya, the rain-cloud that quenches all thirst; Pavana, the purifying wind; Anila, the breath that needs no prompting; Amṛtāṃśa, whose portion is nectar; Amṛtavapus, of immortal body; Sarvajña, the omniscient; and Sarvatomukha, whose faces are turned in every direction.
